title: Sheaves of rings are ring objects of abelian sheaves
statement:
In the situation of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-presheaf], let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of rings on
$C$. Then its underlying abelian presheaf $\mathcal R_{\Ab}$ is a sheaf, and it carries a unique
ring object structure in $\Sh(C,\Ab)$ such that the counit isomorphism
$a(\mathcal R_{\Ab})\cong\mathcal R_{\Ab}$ is an isomorphism of ring objects, where
$a(\mathcal R_{\Ab})$ has the structure of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-presheaf]. Concretely, its
multiplication $\mathcal R_{\Ab}\otimes\mathcal R_{\Ab}=a(\mathcal R_{\Ab}\otimes_p\mathcal R_{\Ab})\to\mathcal R_{\Ab}$
is the unique morphism of sheaves extending the objectwise ring multiplication, and its unit
$\underline{\mathbf Z}\to\mathcal R_{\Ab}$ is the unique morphism extending $n\mapsto n\cdot1$. It is
commutative when all rings $\mathcal R(U)$ are commutative, and a morphism of sheaves of rings is
a morphism of ring objects.

proof.text: The forgetful functor from rings to abelian groups is a right adjoint, by the tensor-algebra adjunction (Mathlib.Algebra.Category.AlgCat.TensorAlgebra). Thus it preserves limits of every size. Apply hasSheafCompose_of_preservesLimitsOfSize to obtain the underlying abelian sheaf, without any relation between the site and coefficient universes.

source.place: Tag 00YR, section-sheaves-algebraic-structures, assertion (alpha) and the description of rings as sextuples

proof.text: Use the sheafification universal property of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], with values in abelian groups. Write $t_F:F\to iaF$ for its universal map. The identity of $iS$ extends uniquely to $e:a(iS)\to S$, so $i(e)t_{iS}=1_{iS}$. Since the inclusion is full, $t_{iS}$ itself is a sheaf morphism $q:S\to a(iS)$. Then $eq=1_S$, while $qe=1_{a(iS)}$: both latter maps have the same composite with $t_{iS}$, and uniqueness of extension proves equality. Hence $e$ is the counit isomorphism and $i(q)=t_{iS}$. Naturality, to be used below, follows from the same uniqueness: for $h:F\to G$, $i(ah)t_F=t_Gh$, since both sides are the extension data defining $ah$. In Lean the counit IsIso instance of the fully faithful inclusion supplies exactly this fact.

source.place: First paragraph, counit isomorphism; Stacks Tags 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint) and 00YR, assertion (epsilon)

proof.text: Let $P=iS$ be the abelian presheaf underlying $\mathcal R$. Apply [det-def-sfb-ring-object-presheaf] to this presheaf of rings. It gives the ring object $A=aP$, with multiplication $m=a(\mu_p)\circ c_{P,P}$ and unit $u=a(\eta_p)$, where $\mu_p:P\otimes_pP\to P$ and $\eta_p:\underline{\mathbf Z}_p\to P$ are the objectwise ring maps, $c_{P,P}:aP\otimes aP\xrightarrow{\sim}a(P\otimes_pP)$ is the strong monoidal comparison, and the unit of the sheaf category is $a(\underline{\mathbf Z}_p)$. It also gives commutativity of $A$ when the section rings are commutative, and preservation of ring-object structures by the sheafification of any presheaf ring morphism. Use the existing upstream Sheaf.monObj_presheafToSheaf_obj and Sheaf.monObj_sheafCompose_obj, rather than introducing any new construction.

source.place: First paragraph, ring-object structure on the sheafification from det-def-sfb-ring-object-presheaf

proof.text: Define $\mu=e\circ m\circ(q\otimes q)$ and $\eta=e\circ u$, using $e:A\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ and $q=e^{-1}$ from step 2. Check the equations of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid] explicitly. If $Q=((q\otimes q)\otimes q)$, cancellation of $qe$ and tensor functoriality give $\mu(\mu\otimes1_S)=e\,m(m\otimes1_A)Q$; naturality of the associator gives $\mu(1_S\otimes\mu)\alpha_S=e\,m(1_A\otimes m)\alpha_AQ$. These agree by associativity of $m$. The left unit composite is $\mu(\eta\otimes1_S)=e\,m(u\otimes1_A)(1_{\mathbf1}\otimes q)=e\lambda_A(1_{\mathbf1}\otimes q)=\lambda_S$, by naturality of the unitor; the right unit composite is $e\,m(1_A\otimes u)(q\otimes1_{\mathbf1})=e\rho_A(q\otimes1_{\mathbf1})=\rho_S$. Also $\mu(e\otimes e)=em$ and $\eta=eu$, so $e$ is a ring-object morphism; the inverse identities $q\mu=m(q\otimes q)$ and $q\eta=u$ make $q$ one as well. Any other structure making $e$ a morphism must satisfy these same two equations, and cancellation of $e\otimes e$ forces precisely $\mu=e m(q\otimes q)$ and $\eta=eu$. This proves the required uniqueness. The Lean witness is Sheaf.monObj_sheafCompose_obj. MonObj.ofIso_one and MonObj.ofIso_mul give the two displayed transport formulas. Any competing structure has the same multiplication by its transport formula, and MonObj.ext then identifies the entire structure, including its unit.

source.place: First paragraph, explicit conjugation, its axioms and uniqueness

proof.text: Use the existing generic lemmas Sheaf.μ_comp_map_mul and Sheaf.ε_comp_map_one from WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.Sites.MonObj. The chosen structure is definitionally Sheaf.monObjOfPresheaf on the underlying abelian sheaf, so these lemmas give precisely the multiplication and unit extension equations. Given any other extension, compose its equation with the reverse of the corresponding canonical extension equation. Sheaf.tensor_hom_ext and Sheaf.unit_hom_ext respectively then prove equality of the extensions. These lemmas already establish the strong-monoidal comparison calculation and the sheafification Hom uniqueness argument, so no separate tensor-local-isomorphism theorem is needed here.

source.place: First paragraph, concrete multiplication and unit; canonical comparison of det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure

proof.text: If every section ring is commutative, step 3 gives $m\beta_{A,A}=m$. Naturality of the sheaf symmetry and the formula of step 4 imply $\mu\beta_{S,S}=e\,m(q\otimes q)\beta_{S,S}=e\,m\beta_{A,A}(q\otimes q)=\mu$. This is exactly the commutativity condition of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid]. No commutativity assumption was used in the construction or the associativity and unit checks. This is the existing theorem Sheaf.isCommMonObj_sheafCompose_obj, applied to the supplied sectionwise commutativity hypothesis.

Apply the existing upstream instance Sheaf.isMonHom_sheafCompose_map. Its proof identifies the underlying sheaf morphism with the sheafification of the ring-presheaf morphism conjugated by the two counit isomorphisms, using counit naturality. Sheafification and the two transported counit isomorphisms are morphisms of monoid objects, and their composite is one as well. This proves both the unit and multiplication compatibility equations for exactly the canonical structures in the statement.

source.place: Second paragraph, preservation of multiplication and unit by sheaf ring morphisms, using the equivalent unique-extension argument
